summary: Okta SCIM displayName normalization prevents approval routing for Support Approval Portal
description:
Issue summary: Several approver assignments in the Support Approval Portal are not routing to the expected users after Okta SCIM syncs. The portal shows requests in state 'Pending - unassigned' even though approvers exist in Okta and are listed on the team roster.

Impact: Support engineers cannot approve certain temporary access and runbook elevation requests. Approx. 4-6% of approval requests in prod-us-east since 2026-03-08 06:00 UTC have been affected. This blocks oncall escalation and is causing manual triage by CS.

Environment: Production (support-approval-portal), region us-east, Okta org: redwood-prod.okta.com, SCIM provisioning service running in k8s cluster identity-provisioner-prod.

Observed behaviour: Approval routing uses a matching key derived from the incoming SCIM profile (displayName) and an internal approver directory index. After the SCIM sync on 2026-03-08, a normalization step removed certain unicode characters and truncated displayName fields to 64 chars; this broke lookup keys for a subset of approvers and caused the approval-queue to treat them as missing.

Why this is likely a SCIM/transformer issue: Historical routing used email or Okta ID; a recent rollout of the 'displayName-first' fallback (see rollout note) caused routing to prefer normalized displayName when email match fails. The normalization logic was updated to remove diacritics and collapse whitespace which leads to collisions or mismatches for names containing non-ascii characters or long compound names.

Immediate business impact: Manual approvals increased volume for the Support queue; an on-call had to approve 12 requests manually in a 2-hour window. No data exfiltration or elevated privilege creation observed; this is an availability/operational correctness issue.

Next steps requested: Triage mapping logic, add temporary fallback to email-based matching, add a hotfix to identity-provisioner to stop truncating displayName or to persist original Okta ID for routing.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Create a test Okta user with a displayName containing diacritics or a long compound name (e.g., 'José María-Alvarez de la Torre, Sr.').
2) Ensure SCIM provisioning maps displayName -> approverKey in identity-provisioner with normalization enabled.
3) Trigger a sample approval flow in support-approval-portal for a request that should route to that approver group.
4) Observe that the approval is left in 'Pending - unassigned' and the portal audit shows 'no approver matched for key: <normalized_displayName>'.
5) Compare Okta SCIM Provisioning Logs and the identity-provisioner transform logs to see the pre/post normalization values.

2026-03-08T07:03:12Z okta-scim WARN response 200 but provisioned=false user=00u1abcde scimErr="normalized name collision"
investigation_notes: 2026-03-10 09:15 - Maya Chen: Initial customer-facing triage. Confirmed affected requests and compiled sample request IDs. Escalated to identity eng and SRE.
2026-03-10 10:02 - Arjun Patel: Reproduced locally using a long displayName. Identity-provisioner transform step contains a new normalizer deployed 2026-03-06 (rev: idp-transform:v3.4.1).

2026-03-10 11:40 - Lena Rivera (SRE): Checked Okta SCIM push logs. Provisioning responses show 200 but a 'provisioned=false' flag for impacted users due to duplicate normalized key detection in internal cache.

2026-03-10 13:05 - Omar Khalid (Identity Eng): Found recent change in PR #1783 that added ascii-folding and truncation to 64 chars. That PR did not add a stable secondary key (oktaUserId) to the approver index.
comments: 2026-03-10 09:20 - Maya Chen: Customer reports started at ~2026-03-08 06:00 UTC after nightly sync. I'm adding request IDs and sample user profiles to the ticket. (refs: slack #support and #idp)

2026-03-10 10:05 - Arjun Patel: I can reproduce with a dev deployment. Temporary mitigation: flip config to prefer email-based matching. Will prepare a config toggle and patch for identity-provisioner.
2026-03-10 12:00 - Lena Rivera: Oncall confirmed manual approvals increased. Pager duty incident #INC-20260308-3 linked in #support. No high error rate in API, just many pending unassigned items.

2026-03-10 14:30 - Omar Khalid: Proposed hotfix: (a) back out normalization truncation from idp-transform:v3.4.1, (b) persist oktaUserId as primary lookup key, (c) add telemetry to detect future collisions. Preparing PR.
2026-03-11 08:12 - Arjun Patel: Deployed config toggle to prefer email matching in prod-us-east at 2026-03-11T08:00Z. Observed drop in unassigned approvals from 5.3% -> 0.4% over the hour.
2026-03-12 09:45 - Maya Chen: Customer-facing update sent: workaround in place, engineering working on permanent fix.
next_steps: 1) Merge PR to persist oktaUserId as primary lookup and remove truncation from normalization. 2) Deploy idp-transform:v3.4.2 with migration script to reindex approvers. 3) Add integration test for names with diacritics. 4) Postmortem scheduled after fix rollout.
workaround: Toggled identity-provisioner to prefer email-based approver matching (rolled back the displayName-first fallback). Support to manually assign pending approvals per runbook until reindex completes.
